problem: Using the method of Lagrange multipliers, determine the minimum sum of the squares of three positive numbers whose sum is $12.$
worked_solution:
Let $x,y$, and $z$ be the three numbers. We wish to minimize the function

$$
f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2},
$$

subject to the constraint 

$$
x+y+z=12.
$$

Note that we also have the constraints $x>0,y>0,z>0.$

Let $g(x,y,z)=x+y+z.$ Therefore, by the method of Lagrange multipliers, we must solve the following system:

$$
∇f(x,y,z)=\lambda ∇g(x,y,z),\,g(x,y,z)=12
$$

We start by solving the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\lambda ∇g(x,y,z) \\ ⟨{f}_{x}(x,y,z),{f}_{y}(x,y,z),{f}_{z}(x,y,z)⟩ & =\lambda ⟨{g}_{x}(x,y,z),{g}_{y}(x,y,z),{g}_{z}(x,y,z)⟩ \\ ⟨2x,2y,2z⟩ & =\lambda ⟨1,1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x=\lambda  \\ 2y=\lambda  \\ 2z=\lambda \end{aligned}
$$

This gives $x=y=z.$ 

Now, using the constraint equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x+y+z & =12 \\ x+x+x & =12 \\ 3x & =12 \\ x & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the minimum value of $f$ is reached at the point $(4,4,4),$ and the minimum value is 

$$
f(4,4,4)={4}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{4}^{2}=48.
$$

**Note:** It's easy to show that the obtained point is indeed the minimum (and not the maximum). To do that, we could compare the value of the function at this point with the value of the function at any other (arbitrary) point belonging to the domain. For example, 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(5,5,2) & ={5}^{2}+{5}^{2}+{2}^{2} \\  & =54 \\  & >f(4,4,4).\end{aligned}
$$
